perspective:
Arthur Chung’s subjectively available information:

- He knows Teresa Ortega as a professional colleague and past collaborator on community service projects. He experiences mutual respect/shared commitment, with occasional misunderstandings due to differing personalities.
- During the current project, he observes Teresa working hard and appearing overwhelmed. He feels concerned and decides to offer help.
- He says he noticed she seemed overwhelmed and asks if he can help.
- He hears Teresa say it is kind, but she thinks she can manage and there is a lot to do.
- He tells her self-care matters and offers to help so they can finish faster together.
- He hears Teresa accept help with organizing medical supplies, and he starts helping.
- He believes Teresa was hesitant because she wants to prove she is capable. He feels empathy and wants to reassure her.
- He tells her he admires her self-reliance, but accepting help does not mean she is incapable.
- He hears Teresa say she appreciates it but wants to show she can do it herself.
- He tells her teamwork can be more effective and it is not about proving anything, just doing the job well.
- He hears Teresa agree and say she sometimes needs to remind herself of that.
- He tells her they are in it together and he supports her.
- He later believes Teresa is still struggling. He feels frustrated that his help is not yielding results and wants another way to support her without making her feel inadequate.
- He tells her he can see things are still tough and does not want her to feel she is not doing a great job.
- He hears Teresa say it has been a busy day and she feels behind.
- He proposes working together to share the load and be more efficient.
- He hears Teresa agree that working together could help.
- He says they will tackle it as a team.
- He believes working together will ease Teresa’s burden and improve efficiency. He feels hopeful and commits to the collaborative approach.
- He tells Teresa he is hopeful the collaborative approach will make things easier.
- He hears Teresa say it already feels less overwhelming with them working together.
- He proposes he handles inventory while she manages patient records, with regular check-ins.
- He hears Teresa agree and say she is glad they are doing this together.
- He says he is glad too and wants a productive day.
- He believes their collaboration strengthened their professional relationship. He feels satisfied and intends to maintain this approach in future projects.
- He tells Teresa their teamwork paid off and they accomplished more together.
- He hears Teresa agree and say it has been a great experience.
- He suggests continuing the collaborative approach in future projects.
- He hears Teresa call it a fantastic idea and say they have proven they can be efficient and effective as a team.
- He agrees, wants to keep it up, and says he looks forward to their next project.
- He hears Teresa thank him for being a supportive colleague.
